items.title: Govt mulls tighter regulations to control influx of foreign e-commerce products
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will consider introducing stricter regulations to control the entry of cheap goods through international e-commerce platforms, especially from China, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, said the influx of foreign products affects the macro economy and directly undermines the competitiveness of local entrepreneurs. However, Anwar said the government will not completely block or restrict these foreign platforms, but the quality and standards of the products sold must be monitored, including their halal status.

items.title: GE16 must be held before February 2028
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 16th General Election (GE16) must be held before February 2028, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, suggesting it could take place before or after National Day next year. Asked what a new mandate would mean for his administration, Anwar said the make-up of the next government would depend on the support voters gave each party. He said religious outreach must be grounded in knowledge and warned that people could mistake political opinions for definitive religious rulings.

items.title: Fadhlina: Students must master basics alongside AI literacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry is committed to teaching teachers and students to use artificial intelligence (AI) ethically and responsibly, while ensuring they continue to master basic skills such as reading, writing and arithmetic. "However, educating children about AI also means educating them about the ethics of its use," she said in a Facebook post. Fadhlina said she had accompanied Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to the launch of the National Education Artificial Intelligence (AI) Initiative, dubbed AI Temu AI, today.

items.title: Basic treatment fees at public health facilities to stay unchanged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Basic treatment fees at public hospitals and clinics should stay at current rates to avoid burdening low-income patients, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said tonight. He said there was no basis for raising the fees because wages had yet to keep pace with economic growth and the cost of living. "Even though inflation is low, should we raise taxes or fees for ordinary people?

items.title: Govt mulls stricter checks on imported online goods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is looking at measures to ensure imported products sold through e-commerce platforms meet minimum quality and safety standards, in a move to protect consumers and ensure fair competition for local manufacturers. Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the matter was discussed with Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali to address the growing availability of imported products sold online without proper quality certification. Some of these products are cheap but do not have quality certification or even Sirim certification.

items.title: 16 organ transplants performed in five days following four donations
items.summary: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the donations involved Universiti Sains Malaysia Hospital, Melaka Hospital, Shah Alam Hospital and Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Baru. He said the generosity of the donors and their families had given patients a second chance at life, enabling eight kidney transplants, three liver transplants, one heart transplant and four corneal transplants. Selayang Hospital and Kuala Lumpur Hospital each carried out four kidney transplants.

items.title: Jom Bantu CSR initiative focuses on environmental conservation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Thirty native trees were planted and 700 lampam fish fingerlings released into Tasik Metropolitan Kepong under the latest Jom Bantu corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative. Karnival Jom Heboh project director Eileen Lim said the initiative, supported by Affin Bank, expanded the scope of the carnival's CSR programme to include environmental conservation. "Jom Bantu is a corporate social responsibility initiative carried out every time Karnival Jom Heboh takes place in different states.

items.title: Examinations Board: No leak in SPM Pendidikan Moral paper
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The alleged leak of the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) Pendidikan Moral examination paper does not meet the definition of an examination leak under the National Assessment Policy, the Examinations Board said. The board said its checks found that the social media post was uploaded at 11.44am, after the examination ended at 10.45am. It said the examination paper was a classified document with confidential status.

items.title: Anwar remembers A. Samad Said's courage, love for language and literature
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim remembers National Laureate Datuk Seri A. Samad Said for his steadfast principles and deep love for language and literature. Rest in peace, Pak Samad. Al-Fatihah," he said.

items.title: BFood narrows quarterly loss to RM4.66mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Berjaya Food Bhd's (BFood) net loss narrowed to RM4.66 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), from RM14.80 million a year earlier. This followed BFood's store rationalisation and cost management initiatives. Despite operating fewer stores in Malaysia during the quarter, the group said it recorded marginally higher revenue.

items.title: No plans to dissolve Pahang state assembly, says Wan Rosdy
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail today said there were no plans to dissolve the state legislative assembly to pave the way for a state election. "There are no plans as of today," he said briefly at the Pahang state assembly sitting at Wisma Sri Pahang. Shafik Fauzan also said he had no intention of defending the Inderapura state seat in the next general election (GE16).

items.title: Malaysia ready to assist disaster-hit Asean countries, says Zahid
items.summary: TANGERANG: Malaysia is ready to assist Asean member states affected by disasters, as well as support efforts to jointly mobilise humanitarian aid beyond the region, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Delivering Malaysia's statement at the 14th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Management (AMMDM) in Jakarta today, Zahid, who is also Central Disaster Management Committee chairman, said disaster preparedness must begin before a tragedy strikes. He said Malaysia was strengthening disaster preparedness through the development of State Disaster Risk Reduction Strategies under the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2030.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 25, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Better performance Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim vows to improve government performance with over a year left in its term. Drug coordinator Police said an RMAF pilot arrested over a RM4.83 million drug haul at Subang airbase allegedly acted as the syndicate's coordinator and transporter. Gag order The court has barred parties in Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain's assault case from making public statements until proceedings conclude.

items.title: 10-hour closure of Lekas Highway for cycling event
items.summary: KAJANG: The entire Kajang-Seremban Highway (Lekas) will be closed to traffic for 10 and half hours from 6pm on Nov 28 to 4.30am the following day for the RHB Lekas Highway Ride 2026. The closure is in conjunction with the 11th edition of the annual cycling event, which will involve nine interchanges and 20 entry and exit ramps along the highway, from Kajang Selatan to Paroi. Lekas chief executive officer Chua Lay Hoon said the company had obtained the support and approval of the Works Ministry, Malaysian Highway Authority, Malaysia Sports Commissioner and police to facilitate the event.

items.title: Cahya Mata posts RM9.05mil net profit in Q3, RM55.57mil for nine months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Cahya Mata Sarawak Bhd posted a net profit of RM9.05 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, compared with RM32.12 million a year earlier. Revenue from the cement division rose 9.2 per cent to RM197.93 million from RM181.17 million. For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, Cahya Mata's net profit rose to RM55.57 million from RM46.13 million a year earlier, while revenue grew 14.3 per cent to RM912.2 million from RM798.4 million.

items.title: Man with hearing difficulties killed after being run over by train in Tenom
items.summary: The victim was found underneath a carriage of a train travelling from Beaufort to Tenom. Tenom Fire and Rescue chief Mudi Pengiran said the department received a call from police about the incident at 1.20pm. Six firefighters were deployed to the scene.

items.title: George Kent swings back to profit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: George Kent (Malaysia) Bhd returned to profitability in the first half ended Sept 30, 2026 (FY27) with a net profit of RM632,000, compared to a net loss of RM7.16 million a year earlier. George Kent's revenue for the six months ended Sept 30, 2026, rose 0.8 per cent to RM86.72 million from RM86.02 million previously. However, for the second quarter ended FY27, the group's net profit fell 62.3 per cent to RM353,000 from RM937,000 a year earlier.

items.title: PPB Group returns to the black with RM271.18mil net profit in Q3
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PPB Group Bhd returned to the black in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026) after recording a net profit of RM271.18 million against a net loss of RM199.55 million in Q3 2025. For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, the group reported a higher net profit of RM843.29 million, compared to RM456.11 million last year. Its film exhibition and distribution segment revenue for Q3 2026 and 9M 2026 increased by 26 per cent to RM208 million and two per cent to RM518 million respectively.

items.title: 14 MoH staff, driver escape unhurt as bus catches fire on highway
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Fourteen people, including 13 Health Ministry (MoH) staff and a driver, escaped unhurt after a ministry-owned bus caught fire near the Senawang southbound rest and recreation (R&R) area today. Seremban Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Fazli Ali said the department received an emergency call at noon and dispatched a fire engine, which arrived at the scene at 12.16pm. Fazli said 19 firefighters and two officers took part in the operation, involving two Fire Rescue Tenders, a water tanker and a four-wheel-drive vehicle from the Senawang, Seremban and Seremban 2 fire and rescue stations.

items.title: Govt allocates RM540,000 to help 54 families affected by Nepal tragedy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has approved RM540,000 in special assistance for 54 Malaysian families affected by the floods and landslides in Nepal on Aug 26. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said each family would receive a one-off payment. He said the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) had channelled RM174,000 in aid to 28 eligible families of contributors on Nov 4, while the latest allocation would cover all 54 families affected by the tragedy.

items.title: No more visa-free entry for Indians from Jan 1 as Malaysia tightens pre-arrival checks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia has announced that the visa exemption for Indian nationals ends on Jan 1, 2027. From that date, Indian nationals must obtain a valid visa before entering Malaysia. “Indian nationals entering Malaysia from that date must obtain a valid visa before arrival,” the statement read.

items.title: EPB's Q3 profit rises 17.6pct as earnings recovery continues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: EPB Group Bhd's net profit rose 17.6 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM2.07 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM1.76 million in the preceding quarter, extending its earnings recovery for the third consecutive quarter. EPB's revenue increased 12 per cent to RM27.75 million from RM24.78 million. Revenue from Indonesia rose to RM8.38 million from RM6.16 million in the preceding quarter.

items.title: CCK's Q3 profit hit by Indonesia factory fire, exports
items.summary: Pre-tax profit fell to RM22.2 million from RM27.2 million in the corresponding quarter last year. CCK also recorded a 22 per cent decline in prawn revenue to RM23.1 million from RM29.6 million. For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, its revenue declined 4.9 per cent to RM747.9 million from RM786.9 million, while pre-tax profit fell to RM49.2 million from RM79.4 million.

items.title: LCS2 to get revised delivery schedule next year after LCS1 delay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Delivery of the second Littoral Combat Ship (LCS2) will be pushed back following delays to the first vessel. Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari said the delay in the delivery of LCS1, which is now scheduled for April, would affect LCS2 but would not disrupt the schedules for LCS3, LCS4 and LCS5. "LCS2 will have a revised schedule, (but) still next year.

items.title: Pernas transfer to Domestic Trade Ministry a cabinet decision, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The transfer of Perbadanan Nasional Bhd (Pernas) from the Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Ministry to the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry was made following a cabinet decision. Deputy Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Datuk Mohamad Alamin said the cabinet, at meetings on Dec 17 last year and Jan 9 this year, had decided to transfer Pernas, along with the development and regulatory functions of the franchise industry. He said despite the transfer, his ministry would continue to work closely with Pernas and other ministries to support entrepreneurship development.

items.title: Ramanan says Nepal tragedy families may get long-awaited closure with death certificates due in December
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Certificates of presumed death for the victims of the flood and landslide tragedy in Nepal are expected to be issued as early as December, once the authorities in that country provide the relevant documentation to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the National Registration Department (NRD) will carry out the issuance process as soon as it receives the verification documents from the Government of Nepal. Also present were SOCSO chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr. Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed, co-founder of Solidariti Malaysia: Keluarga Dalam Harapan (Masfih) Dr. Manivannan Rethinam, and family members of the tragedy’s victims.

items.title: Netizens outraged as three men accused of assaulting elderly man seen laughing outside court [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Netizens have expressed outrage over the conduct of three men remanded over an alleged road-rage assault on a 62-year-old man, after they were seen laughing and smiling outside court today. Another said the three should be put behind bars over the alleged assault. Their demeanour was captured by media practitioners gathered outside the court, following the circulation of footage showing the alleged assault on social media.

items.title: Ko-Khawan discontinues special investment scheme, SKM probes funds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Co-operative Societies Commission (SKM) is examining the flow of funds and investments of Koperasi Khazanah Usahawan (Ko-Khawan) Berhad following the discontinuation of its special investment scheme. "The special investment scheme has been discontinued and the cooperative is no longer accepting new investments under the scheme. "SKM initiated an audit of the cooperative on April 13 under Section 64 of the Co-operative Societies Act.

items.title: Infant hospitalised after being picked up from babysitter’s home, police launch probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Police are investigating a neglect case involving a five-month-old baby girl who was found unconscious and suffering from seizures after being picked up by her mother from a babysitter’s home recently. Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said that in addition to seizures, preliminary examinations on the infant also revealed bruises and wounds on her face and ears. He said police received a report regarding the incident from a medical officer at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) after the victim’s mother brought the baby to the hospital’s Emergency Department for treatment on Nov 14.

items.title: After RM4.8m meth bust, Mindef moves to protect RMAF personnel who made arrests
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The Ministry of Defence (Mindef) is protecting Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel who arrested suspects in a drug trafficking syndicate that used military transport facilities in the Klang Valley and Labuan recently. Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari said the ministry will shield all RMAF personnel cooperating with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) in further investigations. Last week, police busted a drug trafficking syndicate using military transport facilities in operations across the Klang Valley and Labuan, seizing 96.64 kg of methamphetamine valued at RM4.83 million and 6.98 kg of liquid chemical.

items.title: Ringgit ends slightly lower as investors await US PCE inflation data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed slightly lower versus the US dollar on the back of growing risk appetite for the greenback ahead of the personal consumption expenditure (PCE) inflation data. At 6pm, the local currency was at 4.1170/1220 against the US dollar compared with yesterday's close of 4.1135/1175. Similarly, core PCE is expected to increase to 3.2 per cent from 3.1 per cent, he said.

items.title: MoE warns of rising anaemia, persistent stunting among students
items.summary: BATU KAWAN: The Education Ministry has warned of rising anaemia risks and persistent stunting among students, calling for stronger nutrition interventions in schools nationwide. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said health data shared by the Health Ministry's Nutrition Division pointed to worrying nutritional gaps, particularly among adolescents who did not have adequate diets or consume enough milk and protein. Fadhlina said the ministry was strengthening primary school nutrition initiatives, including the Supplementary Food Programme (RMT) and the Healthy Eating in Schools (HiTS) programme.

items.title: ‘When others were silenced, Pak Samad fought back with poetry,’ says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he will always remember the late National Laureate Datuk Seri A. Samad Said’s steadfastness in upholding his principles and his deep love for language and literature. Rest in peace, Pak Samad. Al-Fatihah,” he said.

items.title: ‘No plans as of today’: Wan Rosdy dismisses talk of early Pahang election
items.summary: KUANTAN, Nov 25 — Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail today said he had no plans to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) to pave the way for a state election. “There are no plans as of today,” he said briefly at the Pahang State Legislative Assembly sitting at Wisma Sri Pahang here. He was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man (PN-Cheka), who wanted to know whether the Pahang DUN would be dissolved following remarks by several assemblymen suggesting that the current sitting could be their last.

items.title: Sunway's Q3 net profit dips 7.1pct to RM314.06mil on higher costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Bhd's net profit fell 7.1 per cent to RM314.06 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM338.14 million a year earlier, weighed down by higher finance costs and taxation. The property development segment's revenue fell 13.6 per cent to RM329.2 million from RM380.9 million a year earlier, mainly due to lower progress billings from local development projects. Meanwhile, the construction segment's revenue fell 33.7 per cent to RM778 million from RM1.17 billion, as certain data centre projects had reached their peak construction activity in earlier periods.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM NOV 25, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia bucked the regional trend to close marginally higher on Wednesday, supported by selective buying in heavyweight counters. The benchmark index inched up 0.61 points or 0.03 per cent, to 1,562.29 from Tuesday's close. In the crypto market, Bitcoin fell to RM242,531.

items.title: Private university student claims trial over Jalan Jelatek crash that killed retired military personnel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — A private university student pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court today to a charge of reckless driving that resulted in the death of a retired military personnel on Jalan Jelatek here last Saturday. The accused, a 32-year-old Libyan national, Ali Abdul Rahman Mahmoud Elmaki, entered his plea after the charge was read to him in English before Magistrate Amalina Johar. “However, should the court choose to exercise its discretion to grant bail under Section 388 of the Criminal Procedure Code, the prosecution proposes bail at RM70,000 with two Malaysian sureties.

items.title: Tides rising, storms brewing: Penang residents advised to monitor weather closely
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 25 — Residents in low-lying areas and near the coast have been advised to increase their level of preparedness following the forecast of high tides, rain and thunderstorms in most areas of the state until Friday (Nov 27). Mohamad Shoki said rain is expected in several areas tomorrow morning, before thunderstorms hit most parts of the state in the afternoon, followed by rain at night. He said similar weather conditions are forecast for Friday, with no rain expected in the morning, before thunderstorms hit most places in the afternoon and rain at night.

items.title: Pantai Remis teen charged with murdering newborn daughter, boyfriend admits helping bury infant
items.summary: TAIPING, Nov 25 — A female teenager was brought before the Magistrate’s Court here today on a charge of murdering her newborn baby girl by stabbing the infant last week. Nurul Iman Najiha Abdullah, 19, nodded in understanding when the charge against her was read out before Magistrate R. Prabakaran. Mohamad Aidil pleaded guilty to the charge, while Nurul Iman Najiha pleaded not guilty.

items.title: Fuel prices take a dive: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel all down 25 sen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Retail prices of RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel will all fall by 25 sen per litre from Nov 26 to Dec 2. The retail price of unsubsidised diesel will fall from RM4.72 to RM4.47 per litre. For Budi Diesel, eligible recipients will continue paying RM2.10 per litre against the unsubsidised price of RM4.47 per litre, with the government subsidising RM2.37 per litre, or 53 per cent of the unsubsidised price.

items.title: Terengganu emerges from floods, Selangor braces as evacuee count approaches 1,000
items.summary: In SELANGOR, 958 people from 281 families were sheltering at relief centres this afternoon, up from 819 people from 228 families this morning. All three centres in Sepang opened today, with Dewan Orang Ramai Kampung Dato Ahmad Razali sheltering 122 people, Dewan Orang Ramai Dengkil 49 and Dewan Orang Ramai Taman Gemilang 15. In Kuala Selangor, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato’ Maharaja Lela housed 313 evacuees, Sekolah Rendah Agama Pasangan 158, Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok 108 and Dewan Orang Ramai Bukit Kuching Tengah 30.

items.title: Fisherman pleads not guilty to insulting ‘hadis’, spreading teachings contrary to Islamic law
items.summary: MANJUNG, Nov 25 — A fisherman pleaded not guilty in the Syariah High Court here today to two charges of insulting the hadis and expounding religious teachings contrary to Islamic law about two years ago. According to the first charge, he allegedly insulted the hadis by uttering the words, “Kalau kita pakai hadis itu kata orang. Syariah prosecutor Amir Sabri Zulkipli proposed bail of RM5,000 in one surety for each charge, arguing that offences involving matters of Islamic faith were serious.

items.title: Flood-hit Shah Alam gets immediate relief as Putrajaya rolls out three projects, eyes bigger RM40m fix
items.summary: Deputy Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation Datuk Seri Abdul Rahman Mohamad said the first project involves the construction of a flood wall and the installation of a flap gate at Taman Rashna, at a cost of RM350,000, with completion scheduled for March 17, 2027. The second project entails the construction of an outlet structure, the installation of a flap gate, and the building of a flood wall near the Bukit Raja junction, at a cost of RM199,000, with completion scheduled for Feb 17, 2027. He was responding to a question from Azli Yusof (PH-Shah Alam) regarding the status of flood control plans for the Sungai Rasah Basin, following recent flash flood incidents.

items.title: Three girls found after string of teenage disappearances in Kota Kinabalu, search continues for 16-year-old Olivia Jeffrey
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 25 — Three of the four teenage girls reported missing in separate incidents in the district have been found, with only one still missing. In a statement today, Kota Kinabalu district police headquarters (IPD) said the three girls who have been found are Lorna Palmani, 17, Nadyana Albaser, 16, and Farha Nabila Abdullah, 14. Meanwhile, Olivia Jeffrey, 16, of Taman Richdar, Menggatal, who was reported missing since November 7, has yet to be found, and police are continuing their search for the teenager.

items.title: Banting son charged with mother’s murder, back in court Jan 19 next year
items.summary: KUALA LANGAT, Nov 25 — An unemployed man, 27, has been charged with murdering his mother at a house in Taman Banting Baru, Selangor. S. M. Madavan was charged at the Telok Datok Magistrate’s Court yesterday with murdering V. Kanagavalli, 51, between 2.30am and 3.30am on November 13, Harian Metro reported today. Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Amirul Syafiq Yazid prosecuted.

items.title: Sarawak election: Chong Chong Chieng Jen heads to Kota Sentosa, GPS hopeful Nicholas Wung says Padungan now a ‘level playing field’
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 25 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) Padungan candidate Nicholas Wung Duk Ying said the contest in the constituency would be fairer now that incumbent Chong Chieng Jen has decided to return to his former seat of Kota Sentosa. Wung, who is Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP) Youth chief and acting secretary, said the Sarawak DAP’s decision to instead place Chong’s special assistant Michael Kong Feng Nian in the constituency would make the contest a more “level playing field” in terms of candidate age and seniority. “Having a GPS assemblyman in the Padungan area would allow us to allocate more resources and funding from GPS.

items.title: PKR sits out Sarawak polls, but Lawas chief may not: Zahid Matserudin mulls solo run in Bukit Sari
items.summary: MIRI, Nov 25 — Lawas PKR branch chief Zahid Matserudin is considering contesting the Bukit Sari seat as an independent candidate following his party’s decision not to take part in the 13th Sarawak state election. Zahid, 35 said he had yet to make a final decision as he was still weighing several factors. In the 2021 state election, Awang Tengah secured 6,385 votes and a majority of 5,636, defeating Alias Mail of the now-defunct Parti Sarawak Bersatu, who polled 749 votes, and Parti Bumi Kenyalang’s Riyah Basra, who received 165 votes.

items.title: ‘Zero opposition’ a no-go, Chong Chieng Jen says as DAP fields 12 candidates in Sarawak polls
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 25 — Sarawak DAP will contest the 13th Sarawak election despite its Pakatan Harapan ally PKR deciding to sit out the polls. Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen said the party had the autonomy to decide what was best for Sarawak and remained committed to providing a stronger opposition to keep the ruling Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) in check. For this coming election, DAP has finalised a 12-seat line-up, comprising Kota Sentosa, Batu Lintang, Padungan, Pending, Batu Kitang, Batu Kawa, Opar, Tanjong Batu, Pujut, Bukit Assek, Pelawan, and Meradong.

items.title: Malaysia wants more frequent Asean meetings to speed up disaster aid
items.summary: TANGERANG, Nov 25 — Malaysia has proposed that senior Asean officials responsible for disaster management meet more often to improve coordination and speed up aid to member states hit by natural disasters. Ahmad Zahid said Asean member states had shown greater commitment to disaster management than in previous years, particularly in delivering aid on time and coordinating their responses. “All Asean member states should adopt this new technology,” he said.

items.title: Nine districts, nine timetables: Selangor refines prayer times for Muslims from Jan 1
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 25 — Selangor will set prayer times by nine districts instead of three zones from January 1, ahead of Ramadan next year, to make worship timings more accurate for Muslims in the state, Harian Metro reported today. Selangor Mufti Datuk Anhar Opir said the change was prompted partly by complaints and checks showing the Maghrib azan was inconsistent throughout Ramadan, which raised concerns about the validity of Muslims’ fasts. The nine districts are Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Kuala Langat, Hulu Langat and Sepang.

items.title: Malaysia condemns Israeli strikes in Gaza that killed UNRWA staff member, injured three others
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysia has strongly condemned the Zionist Israel regime’s strikes in Gaza on November 23 that killed a staff member of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) and injured three others. “Malaysia calls on the international community to end Israel’s impunity and protect civilians, humanitarian aid workers and United Nations personnel,” the statement read. Anadolu Ajansi reported on November 24 that one UNRWA staff member was killed and three others were injured in an Israeli attack in the Gaza Strip.

items.title: Heavy rain and lightning expected in parts of Perak and East Malaysia until 5pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an afternoon thunderstorm advisory for parts of Perak, Sabah, Sarawak, and the Federal Territory of Labuan, warning of heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 5.00pm today. Across East Malaysia, the advisory blankets widespread southern, coastal, and interior localities in Sarawak, including Kuching, Serian, Sri Aman, and Limbang. The warning concurrently extends across Gedong and Simunjan in the Samarahan division, alongside Song and Kapit in the Kapit division.

items.title: Marine police seize RM5.36m worth of syabu after 90-minute high-speed boat chase off Kedah
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 25 — The Region 1 Marine Police Force (PPM) has crippled a transnational drug smuggling syndicate operating through sea routes following the seizure of over 103 kilogrammes (kg) of syabu (methamphetamine) worth RM5.36 million and the arrest of four men in operations in the waters off Tanjung Dawai and Sungai Petani, Kedah, recently. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (KDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the team conducting patrol at 9pm on November 14 detected a suspicious fibreglass boat about seven nautical miles from Pulau Sayak in the waters off Tanjung Dawai. Following the arrests, he said police raided a house in Kampung Sungai Layar Hujung, Sungai Petani and detained two more men - a Malaysian and an Indonesian - on November 15.

items.title: Bukit Aman warns drug syndicates may target other airports amid tighter KLIA security
items.summary: TUMPAT, Nov 25 — Drug smuggling syndicates could target Sultan Ismail Petra Airport in Kota Bharu following attempts to use other airports since security was tightened at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), Bukit Aman said. “When we tightened security at KLIA, there were attempts to use the airports in Penang and Ipoh. We believe these syndicates will target other airports too,” he said.

items.title: Govt considers naming KL street after A. Samad Said, setting up gallery to honour his legacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The government will consider naming a Kuala Lumpur street after the late National Laureate Datuk Seri A Samad Said and setting up a gallery to showcase his work, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. Fahmi said veteran journalist Datuk A. Kadir Jasin proposed naming the street in recognition of Samad’s contributions to literature and journalism. Fahmi said a gallery was also worth considering as a way to honour Samad and introduce his writing to younger readers.

items.title: Malaysia benefits immensely as a trading nation by engaging with world leaders, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia has benefited immensely as a trading nation, and this is reflected in its engagements with world leaders, particularly during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting held recently in Shenzhen, China. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said he met with US President Donald Trump during the Asean-US Special Summit in Manila, which was held in conjunction with the 49th Asean Summit, as well as Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. So I was quite relieved when President Xi Jinping, President Trump and President Putin sat down together.

items.title: Court grants gag order in border agency chief Shuhaily’s case, media allowed to report proceedings
items.summary: SEPANG, Nov 25 — The Magistrate’s Court today set December 23 for the remention of the case involving the director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, who faces two charges of causing injury to police personnel. Magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani set the date for case management after the defence informed the court that they had received the relevant case documents from the prosecution this morning. Meanwhile, lawyer Datuk Rosal Azimin Ahmad, representing Mohd Shuhaily, said the court had granted an application for a “gag order” against the parties involved in the case.

items.title: Malaysians lost RM7.33b to online scams since 2023, Dewan Rakyat told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysians lost RM7.33 billion to online scams since 2023, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told the Dewan Rakyat today, warning that cyber fraud cases continue to climb with women and private sector employees bearing the brunt. Between January 2023 and October 2026, the authorities recorded 192,869 online scam cases, resulting in 75,266 arrests and 69,665 charges brought to court, the home minister revealed. Authorities have categorised online fraud into six primary modus operandi: telecommunications scams, e-financial crimes, love scams, e-commerce fraud, non-existent loans, and non-existent investment schemes.

items.title: Malaysia must prepare for quantum computing and rogue AI threats, Fahmi says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysia must rapidly upgrade its national cybersecurity defences in lockstep with physical infrastructure investments to shield the country from emerging vulnerabilities posed by quantum computing and autonomous rogue agentic artificial intelligence, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. Addressing the opening of the NEXSEC2026 cybersecurity conference at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC), Fahmi said that the government is prioritising quantum migration and post-quantum cryptography to prevent sensitive data traversing domestic telecommunications networks from being compromised. “This is why I have tasked the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) with convening research and development discussions on quantum migration and quantum-safe communications involving telecommunications companies and infrastructure providers.

items.title: Fresh blood for GPS: 11 new faces in 82-strong Sarawak election line-up
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 25 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) is fielding 11 new faces among the 82 candidates announced by its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg for the 13th Sarawak state election. The revamped line-up, announced at Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) headquarters here, also features five women candidates, reflecting the coalition’s continued efforts to ensure female representation in the state’s political leadership. Abang Johari said the new GPS candidate line-up also sees an increase in women’s representation, with five female candidates being fielded compared to four in the previous state election.
